title: Perfect direct image along a perfect proper morphism
statement: Let Y be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], let f:X\to Y be a perfect proper morphism of schemes (perfect means finite Tor dimension, equivalently that \mathcal O_X has finite Tor dimension over f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y), and let P be a perfect object of D(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Then Rf_*P [def-pc-derived-direct-image] is a perfect object of D(\mathcal O_Y) [def-pc-perfect-complex].

proof.text: Conditions (1)-(3) of Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.27.1 (Tag 08EV) hold, as in Tag 0B6G where (1),(2) are called immediate and (3) local. Because f is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], it is of finite type, hence locally of finite type, X is Noetherian, and X is proper over Y; the support of every cohomology sheaf of P is closed in X, hence proper over Y (a closed immersion followed by f). Locally P is represented by a bounded strictly perfect complex [def-pc-perfect-complex]; on the Noetherian scheme X its cohomology sheaves are coherent, and since X is quasi-compact finitely many opens suffice, so P is bounded with coherent cohomology. The perfect-morphism hypothesis says that O_X has finite Tor dimension over f^{-1}O_Y; each term of a local bounded strictly perfect representative of P is a direct summand of a finite free O_U-module, so the representative has finite Tor dimension over f^{-1}O_Y, and by quasi-compactness of X the bound is uniform, so P has finite Tor dimension over f^{-1}O_Y.

Apply [lem-pc-bounded-coherent-finite-tor-proper-pushforward-perfect] with S=Y and E=P. Its hypotheses (Y Noetherian, f locally of finite type, P bounded with coherent cohomology, supports proper over Y, finite Tor dimension over f^{-1}O_Y) are exactly the conclusions of step 1, so Rf_*P is perfect on Y.
